exposure: fetal head descent (measured by head-perineum distance and angle of progression)
cohort: The study included 46 nulliparous pregnant women undergoing labor.
finding: Occipital transverse is the most common fetal head position in early labor, with rotation mostly occurring in the active and second stages, and fetal head position significantly impacts labor outcomes, including rates of cesarean section, oxytocin use, and epidural analgesia.
mod_finding: All cases with an occipital anterior position resulted in eutocia, while the left transverse occipital group had the highest rate of cesarean section.
